items.message: License EPS threshold exceeded: current 28,400 EPS exceeds licensed 25,000 EPS
items.title: EPS license threshold exceeded
items.technical_explanation: The events-per-second rate received by one or more event processors exceeded the licensed EPS pool or the per-host allocation.
items.root_cause: Event/flow volume exceeding the licensed pool or an invalid/expired licence key.
items.business_impact: Security telemetry is silently lost during peak periods; offenses may not fire and audit evidence can be incomplete.
items.impact: Events above the licensed rate are queued to the temporary 'burst' buffer and, when the buffer is exhausted, are dropped or routed to the 'Dropped Events' log source, causing detection and compliance gaps.
items.risk: High - data loss and potential licence compliance breach.
recommendation: Review the License Pool Management page (Admin > System Configuration > System and License Management) and confirm EPS allocation per managed host.
Identify the top EPS log sources (Log Activity > Group by Log Source) and filter noisy or low-value events with routing rules, custom event properties or at-source tuning.
Rebalance EPS between event processors, or purchase additional EPS capacity / add an Event Processor.
Enable event coalescing for high-volume, repetitive sources and disable payload storage where not required.
items.best_practice: IBM recommends sizing EPS licence at 20-30% above sustained peak and reviewing consumption at least quarterly; avoid sustained operation above 90% of the licensed rate.

items.message: WinCollect agents disconnected: 12 agents have not checked in
items.title: WinCollect agents disconnected / communication problems
items.technical_explanation: Managed WinCollect agents are not checking in with the QRadar Console/Event Collector, or event delivery to the destination fails.
items.root_cause: Agent connectivity, certificate or configuration problem.
items.business_impact: No visibility of Windows authentication, privilege and process activity on affected servers.
items.impact: Windows event logs from the affected hosts are not forwarded; the agents may buffer to disk and later overflow.
recommendation: Verify the agent service is running and that TCP 8413 (agent management) and the event destination port (TCP/UDP 514 or 6514 TLS) are reachable.
Check certificate/token validity for managed agents and the destination definition in the WinCollect app.
Review the agent's WinCollect.log for connection and certificate errors and restart the service if required.
items.best_practice: IBM recommends WinCollect agents in managed mode with TLS-secured syslog to a dedicated Event Collector; monitor agent heartbeats centrally.

items.message: Events were not parsed: Unknown log source type for 14 sources
items.title: Event parsing errors / unparsed events
items.technical_explanation: A significant share of events are unrecognised (Unknown/Stored events) or raise parsing exceptions in the event pipeline.
items.root_cause: Events not matching an installed DSM, DSM out of date or log source mis-typed.
items.business_impact: Detections and compliance reports miss data from the affected sources.
items.impact: Events are stored with generic categories, cannot be used in CRE rules and searches, and consume licence and storage without security value.
recommendation: Use Log Activity > filter 'Log Source Type = Unknown' / 'Event Name = Unknown' to identify the sources.
Install the correct DSM and latest DSM/protocol Auto Update; confirm the log source type and protocol settings.
Where no DSM exists, use the DSM Editor / Universal DSM with LEEF/CEF formatting.
Review 'Parsing Issues' notifications and /var/log/qradar.error for exceptions.
items.best_practice: Keep Unknown/Stored events below 1% of total; review parsing health monthly using the Log Source Management app.

items.message: Managed host qr-ec01 is not responding (hostcontext down)
items.title: Managed host connectivity problem
items.technical_explanation: One or more managed hosts are unreachable from the Console or report an error/inactive state.
items.root_cause: Deployment/connectivity configuration inconsistency or failed update.
items.business_impact: Partial or complete loss of data from components on that host.
items.impact: Configuration cannot be deployed to the host; events/flows from that host may be missing; services may be down.
recommendation: Verify network connectivity and SSH from the Console to the managed host (TCP 22) and that the encryption tunnel (TCP 4333 / 7777) is established.
Check 'hostcontext' and 'tomcat' services on the managed host, system time (NTP) and disk space.
If the host was rebuilt, remove and re-add it, then deploy full configuration.
items.best_practice: Monitor managed host status and keep time synchronised across the deployment.

items.message: Disk usage on /store has exceeded 93% on qr-ep01
items.title: Disk capacity threshold exceeded
items.technical_explanation: A monitored file system (/store, /storetmp, /var/log, /transient, /) has crossed the QRadar disk usage warning/critical threshold.
items.root_cause: Capacity growth or retention misalignment on the affected file system, or storage subsystem latency.
items.business_impact: Event collection outage and loss of historical search; recovery requires emergency clean-up.
items.impact: At 95% QRadar stops accepting events and flows (ecs-ec-ingress / hostcontext halts services) and Ariel searches fail; /var/log or / full can crash PostgreSQL and tomcat.
items.risk: Critical - service outage imminent or ongoing.
recommendation: Identify the largest consumers with 'du -shx /store/* | sort -h' and the /store/ariel retention settings.
Review Ariel retention buckets (Admin > Data Retention) and reduce retention for low-value event/flow categories.
Remove stale files in /store/tmp, /storetmp, old backups and large core/heap dumps; rotate /var/log.
Add storage (expand LVM volume, add a Data Node, or offload to a secondary store) and enable Data Node rebalancing.
Configure disk usage notification thresholds to alert at 80% / 90%.
items.best_practice: IBM recommends keeping /store below 80% with retention aligned to compliance; never run above 90% as the 95% hard stop halts processing.

items.message: Backup failed: unable to write to /store/backup
items.title: Configuration / data backup failure
items.technical_explanation: A scheduled QRadar configuration or data backup failed or has not completed recently.
items.root_cause: Backup target unavailable/full or the backup job failed to complete.
items.business_impact: Extended recovery time and potential permanent configuration loss after a failure.
items.impact: No recent restore point; disaster recovery and upgrade rollback are compromised.
recommendation: Check Admin > Backup and Recovery > View Backup Archives for the failure reason.
Verify free space on the backup location (default /store/backup) or the NFS target and its mount options.
Run an on-demand backup and test a restore in a lab; ensure retention and schedule are configured.
items.best_practice: IBM recommends nightly configuration backups stored off-box, with periodic restore tests and backups taken before every upgrade.

items.message: Auto update failed: unable to connect to the update server public.dhe.ibm.com
items.title: Auto Update failed
items.technical_explanation: The Auto Update process failed to download or install DSM, protocol, vulnerability or configuration updates.
items.root_cause: Deployment/connectivity configuration inconsistency or failed update.
items.business_impact: Reduced detection coverage and growing technical debt in log source parsing.
items.impact: DSM and protocol fixes are not applied, causing parsing errors and unrecognised events; security content becomes stale.
recommendation: Check Admin > Auto Update > View Log and verify connectivity to the IBM update server (public.dhe.ibm.com / FixCentral) over HTTPS/443, including proxy settings.
Check free disk space in /store/tmp and /var/log and that the Console time is correct (NTP).
For air-gapped deployments, apply the Auto Update ZIP manually (Admin > Auto Update > Upload) and schedule a quarterly cadence.
Re-run 'Get New Updates' and confirm the 'Last Successful Update' timestamp.
items.best_practice: IBM recommends enabling Auto Update with weekly schedule and deploying changes after each successful download; review the Auto Update log monthly.

items.title: App Framework / container error
items.technical_explanation: The QRadar Apps Framework (Docker) reports failures starting, installing or running an application container.
items.root_cause: App Framework container fault, resource limit or permission issue.
items.business_impact: Features relying on the application are unavailable to analysts.
items.impact: Installed applications (e.g. Log Source Management, Pulse, UBA, Use Case Manager) are unavailable.
recommendation: Check container state with 'docker ps -a' and logs with 'docker logs <id>' on the App Host/Console.
Validate free space on /store/docker and on the application volume; verify the Docker service and 'qrd' services.
Re-deploy the application or restart via Admin > Apps; verify the minimum QRadar version for the application.
items.best_practice: Dedicate an App Host for production workloads (>3 applications) and keep apps on supported versions.

items.message: HA cluster qr-console01 is not synchronized (DRBD Inconsistent)
items.title: HA failover / synchronisation problem
items.technical_explanation: An HA cluster is not synchronised, is in failed/standalone state or has recently failed over.
items.root_cause: Replication, heartbeat or configuration fault in the HA cluster.
items.business_impact: Loss of redundancy; risk of data loss and extended outage upon the next failure.
items.impact: If the primary fails there is no healthy standby; data on the replica may be stale or inconsistent (split-brain risk).
recommendation: Run 'ha_status'/'drbdadm status' on both nodes and check the DRBD connection and disk state (UpToDate/Inconsistent).
Verify heartbeat and replication network connectivity (ping, MTU, firewall ports 7788-7799).
Resolve split-brain per IBM technical note, then resynchronise the secondary; contact QRadar Support if the cluster cannot recover.
items.best_practice: Monitor HA state continuously, keep both nodes at identical versions and avoid maintenance on both nodes simultaneously.

items.message: Ariel searches are slow: 17 searches queued
items.title: Search performance issues
items.technical_explanation: Ariel searches are slow, queued or timing out.
items.impact: Analysts cannot investigate quickly; reports and dashboards time out.
recommendation: Review long-running and concurrent searches (Log Activity > Search > Manage Search Results).
Create indexes on frequently searched properties and reduce time ranges; use saved searches with aggregated columns.
Review retention, storage latency and CPU/memory on the Event Processors.
items.best_practice: Index heavily used properties, limit concurrent searches per user and schedule large reports off-peak.

items.message: Events dropped: event pipeline queue overflow on qr-ep01
items.title: Event pipeline backlog / dropped events
items.technical_explanation: The event pipeline (ECS) is backlogged or events are being dropped due to queue overflow.
items.root_cause: Event pipeline saturation causing queue overflow.
items.impact: Events are permanently lost; searches show gaps; offense generation is delayed.
recommendation: Check ECS queue stats and 'Dropped Events' in Log Activity; identify the affected collector/processor.
Validate CPU, memory and disk latency on the processor; rebalance sources or add processing capacity.
Review rules/custom properties adding pipeline overhead; apply routing rules to drop noise.
items.best_practice: Size processors with 30% headroom and monitor pipeline queues with alerts.

items.title: Scheduled report generation completed
items.technical_explanation: QRadar generated a system notification that is not mapped to a specific knowledge-base article.
items.root_cause: Deployment/connectivity configuration inconsistency or failed update.
items.impact: Potentially service-affecting; analysis of the notification detail is required.
recommendation: Review the notification detail and the related log under /var/log/qradar.error and /var/log/qradar.log on the reporting host.
Search IBM Support and Technotes for the notification text; open a support case with a get_logs package if unresolved.
items.best_practice: Review and clear system notifications weekly; do not leave unresolved notifications for extended periods.
